summary:
TerraNova is a web platform that finds Earth's "hidden twins" of the Moon and Mars: real places on our planet that resemble lunar and Martian terrain, for astronaut training and equipment testing.

Users pick the Moon, Mars, or both, choose the features that matter (impact craters, lava tubes, anorthosite, basalt, permafrost, glacial ice), and set how much each one counts. TerraNova ranks Earth sites by match percentage and shows the geology, weather forecast, fieldwork readiness, and the papers behind each match. Users can also compare a site with a lunar or Martian landscape in 3D and print a field report.

This answers Challenge 10 directly. Agencies keep returning to the same few analog sites, while many good ones are poorly documented and matching is slow and manual. TerraNova is built on a dataset compiled from 7 research papers: 21 Moon and Mars sites and 45 Earth analog sites, including lesser-known ones in Egypt and North Africa. It runs on open data from NASA, ESA, and Open-Meteo.

It matters because it brings forward accessible, lower-cost sites for training, research, and testing.
details: TerraNova is an interactive platform that finds places on Earth that resemble the Moon and Mars, built for the challenge "Identify Earth Locations that Analog Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars." Key features: Mission Planner: choose the Moon, Mars, or both, pick geological traits (impact craters, lava tubes, anorthosite, basalt, permafrost, glacial ice), and weight each one. Ranked results: 43 curated analog sites ranked by weighted match, showing matched and missing features, with filters by country, classification, and location accuracy. 3D planetary explorer: NASA models of Earth, Moon, and Mars with site markers, plus an Earth map. Side-by-side 3D terrain comparison: Earth sites against lunar or Martian counterparts using NASA Trek and open elevation data, with controls for sun angle, vertical exaggeration, wireframe, flyover, and synchronized cameras. Field reports: printable PDF reports with live Open-Meteo weather, logistics, and risks. Community contributions and a Methodology page, in Arabic and English, with shareable links. Why it matters: choosing the right analog site is central to astronaut training, rover testing, and mission rehearsal. TerraNova makes that choice faster, transparent, and evidence-based, labeling pairings "proposed" and coordinates "approximate" until scientists verify them.
